title: NeoRadar system policy
description: systems/<system>/policy.json: the per-system behaviour policy. Absent means every default, which is the client's existing behaviour. Each domain adds its own section here; every key is optional and documented by what it does, and an absent key keeps the existing behaviour.

correlation.description: How this system decides a track is identified. Every key is optional; an unknown enum value or a malformed code is a load error and the system loads on defaults.

mode.description: Which identification methods this system honours. always correlates every target, which is the existing behaviour.

requireDiscrete.description: A conspicuity, special or emergency code never identifies, even when it is the assigned code.

acceptPilotSquawk.description: When nothing is assigned, a discrete transmitted code is adopted as the assigned code.

doNotCorrelate.description: Codes that never identify, as literals ("7010") or inclusive ranges ("7001-7007").

maxDistanceFromRouteNm.description: Refuse an assigned-code correlation when the target is further than this from the filed route. Skipped when no route geometry is available.

minGroundSpeedKt.description: Apply the conformance gate only at or above this ground speed.

correlateOn.description: anyCode identifies a Mode S aircraft whatever it squawks; conspicuityOnly requires 1000.

unknownEquipment.description: What an equipment string that says nothing about Mode S means. byAircraftClass asks the server, and counts as not capable until it answers.

decorrelateOnCodeChange.description: A code-correlated track drops to uncorrelated when it changes to a code that is not the assigned or an emergency code.

scope.description: network needs the server; without it the check degrades to local.

afterSeconds.description: Position age after which the track coasts. 0 disables coasting.

special.description: Special purpose codes, in addition to the emergency codes.

conspicuity.description: Conspicuity codes, in addition to 1000, 2000, 7000, 7010, 1200 and 1202.

attention.description: How this system decides which aircraft are your concern. Every key is optional; absent means the existing behaviour.

concerned.description: Confirms the Concerned tier over the flight's trajectory builds, so a flight whose successive builds disagree about entering your airspace does not flicker. A build is one the server made, counted once however often it is evaluated. Absent means 1 of 1 both ways: every build's verdict is taken at once, which is the existing behaviour. Intruder and Notified are never confirmed.

enter.description: When a flight not held Concerned becomes Concerned. enter.count plus leave.count must exceed the larger of enter.of and leave.of, so that entering and leaving can never both hold over the same builds; a rule where they can is a load error.

count.description: Concerned is confirmed only when count of the last of trajectory builds of the flight enter your airspace. Must not exceed of. Needs of written beside it.

of.description: How many of the flight's latest trajectory builds count is taken from.

leave.description: When a flight held Concerned stops being Concerned. enter.count plus leave.count must exceed the larger of enter.of and leave.of, so that entering and leaving can never both hold over the same builds; a rule where they can is a load error.

count.description: Concerned is released only when count of the last of trajectory builds of the flight do not enter your airspace. Must not exceed of. Needs of written beside it.

of.description: How many of the flight's latest trajectory builds count is taken from.

coordination.description: How this system runs the coordination dialogue at a sector boundary. Absent means today's behaviour, which is that every level at a boundary is either the one the coordination table states or one a controller proposed by hand, and nothing is ever agreed without a dialogue.

notification.description: Advance boundary information: announcing a flight to the sector it is coming to, ahead of anyone coordinating it, which is what puts it in that controller's inbound list before it is touched. Absent means no notification tier at all, which is the existing behaviour.

leadMinutesBeforeCoordinationPoint.description: How far ahead of the coordination point a flight is announced to the receiving sector. The European regional default is 15. Absent means a flight is never announced ahead of the boundary.

perPoint.description: A different lead time at named coordination points, for a boundary that needs more or less warning than the rest. Keyed by fix name, matched without regard to case; naming one fix twice is a load error.

preDepartureLeadMinutes.description: The pre-departure half of the tier: a flight on the ground at an airport one of your sectors is active for is announced this many minutes before its filed off-block time, until it is airborne, so it is in the departure list before it moves. Read through isAnnouncedDeparture. Absent means no departure is announced ahead of off-block.

release.description: Release: letting the controller who takes the flight next turn, climb or descend it before the transfer of control point without asking. Absent means this system does no releases at all, which is the existing behaviour.

enabled.description: Whether a controller may release a flight on this system. The kinds are always turn, climb and descent, each optionally bounded by a level.

pointOut.description: Point-out: the controller working a flight drawing another controller's attention to it, with nothing asked in return. Absent means this system does no point-outs, which is the existing behaviour and leaves a plugin's prenotes alone.

enabled.description: Whether a controller may point a flight out on this system. It goes as an OLDI PNT to a controller who has advertised OLDI and as the legacy #PC CCP:PT point-out to anyone else.

holdMinutes.description: How long a point-out stays on the receiving controller's screen. Nothing on the wire ends it, so time does; zero is a load error.

filter.description: The standard versus non-standard filter. A coordination whose level matches the standing agreement and which is made in good time before the coordination point is already agreed, and needs no dialogue; anything else raises one.

acceptanceImplied.description: Treat a standard coordination as agreed without a proposal, which is what a standing agreement is: a written agreement applied automatically, with no exchange between the two controllers. False keeps every change a dialogue, which is the existing behaviour.

standardLevels.description: The level the standing agreement states at a coordination point, overriding whatever the sector file's coordination table carries there. Keyed by fix name, matched without regard to case; naming one fix twice is a load error.

climbFt.description: The agreed level for a flight climbing through the point. Null means the agreement says nothing about a climbing flight.

descendFt.description: The agreed level for a flight descending through the point. Null means the agreement says nothing about a descending flight.

nonStandardAfter.description: How late a coordination may be made and still count as standard. With both keys absent, lateness alone never makes one non-standard.

minutesBeforeCoordinationPoint.description: Inside this many minutes of the coordination point, any coordination is non-standard and raises a dialogue however well its level matches.

distanceNm.description: Inside this distance from the coordination point, any coordination is non-standard. Applied alongside the time limit, whichever is reached first.

surface.description: The surface: what a ground position does on its own. The five SPEC-171 ownership states are always computed and read through surfaceOwnershipState and surfaceResponsibleController; this section switches on the behaviour around them. Absent means every default.

autoAssumeOnClearance.description: EUROCONTROL ITWP Baseline HMI 4.3.17: a push, taxi, line-up or take-off clearance issued to a mobile nobody holds assumes it, so the ground position never assumes as a separate action. Only a ground status THIS controller sets counts; another controller's change never assumes anything here, and a mobile somebody already holds is left alone.

movement.description: Tunes surfaceMovementPhase, the NOVA 9000 TMERS event list read as states (unknown, on stand, pushback, taxiing, holding, on runway, taking off, departed, airborne, approaching, landed). The phase is always computed, every batch, from the zones holding the mobile, its speed, the ground flag and its height above the field, with the previous phase as memory; this block names the zones and moves the thresholds. Absent means every default, which matches the UK zones and the lhr tag thresholds.

standZoneTag.description: The zones.geojson tag that marks a stand area, matched as a whole tag. Empty means no zone counts as a stand, so on stand and pushback are never produced.

runwayZoneTag.description: The zones.geojson tag that marks a runway strip, matched as a whole tag. Empty means no zone counts as a runway, so on runway, taking off and landed are never produced.

movingKts.description: Ground speed at or above which a mobile is moving: taxiing rather than holding, pushback rather than on stand.

rollingKts.description: Ground speed at or above which a mobile on the runway is in a runway movement, taking off or landed, rather than entered, lined up or crossing. Must be above movingKts or the system loads on defaults.

approachAglFt.description: Height above the field below which an airborne, descending mobile is approaching.

departedAglFt.description: Height above the field below which a mobile airborne off a take-off roll is still departed rather than airborne.

runwayMonitoring.description: Runway monitoring, the NOVA 9000 RIMCAS scenarios the data supports. Absent means off. Present, even empty, turns it on with every default: strips from the package's runway zones (tags runway and rwy-09L-27R, LVP twin lvp) else a rectangle from the navdata ends and width, the landing threshold from the navdata end plus displaced threshold. Core publishes rimcasStage, rimcasReason, rimcasRunway, rimcasTimeToRunway, rimcasCountdown and rimcasLowVisibility; the package colours Stage One, flashes Stage Two and lists the Impending Arrival Window. A number that would make the net lie is a load error naming the key.

strip.description: Where the monitored area comes from and how far it reaches.

zoneTag.description: The zones.geojson tag marking a runway strip zone; the zone must also carry the pair tag (runwayTagPrefix plus 09L-27R, either order).

lvpZoneTag.description: The tag marking the low-visibility twin of a runway zone, used while LVP are in force.

runwayTagPrefix.description: The prefix of the pair tag on a runway zone.

sideMarginM.description: Ground metres added each side of the navdata rectangle beyond the runway's half width. Only the navdata fallback uses it; a zone is drawn where the author drew it.

endMarginM.description: Ground metres the navdata rectangle extends beyond each pavement end.

restrictedZoneTag.description: The zones.geojson tag marking a restricted area: any mobile inside one is a Stage Two (rules.restrictedArea). Empty turns the scenario off.

occupancy.description: A mobile inside the area is on the runway unless it is flying over it.

maxGroundSpeedKts.description: An airborne mobile faster than this over the strip is an overflight, not an occupant (vSMR used 160).

maxClimbFpm.description: An airborne mobile climbing faster than this over the strip is an overflight.

maxAglFt.description: An airborne mobile higher than this above the runway is not on it: the local altitude below which an aircraft over the strip is a conflict object. A position that reports no height above ground reads its true altitude less the runway's threshold elevation.

oppositeDirectionDeg.description: Two moving occupants whose headings are within this of opposite, and closing, are head-on (rules.oppositeDirection).

movingKts.description: Below this an occupant is standing: lined up, holding or stopped crossing. Under pairs notBehind, two occupants conflict (rules.occupants) only when one moving has the other AHEAD of it, EUROCONTROL-SPEC-171's 'not behind', so a conditional line-up behind a departure's roll is no conflict.

entryLookaheadS.description: How far ahead a mobile on the ground is predicted along its track for rules.predictedEntry, seconds. No source gives this value; 10 s is a local choice that covers the under 6 s a mobile takes from a close holding point to the runway at 15 kt.

pairs.description: When two occupants of one strip conflict. notBehind is EUROCONTROL-SPEC-171 App A. any is vSMR's and the NOVA 9000's multiple-occupancy rule: any two on one runway are Stage One whatever their geometry, and Stage Two still needs one faster than stageTwoSpeedKts closing on another.

arrival.description: The arrival prediction and its two windows.

lookaheadS.description: How far ahead along the track an approach is searched for, seconds. Must reach stageOneS and stageOneLvpS.

alignmentDeg.description: How far off a runway end's approach bearing a track may be and still count as aligned.

heldAlignmentDeg.description: An aircraft already approaching stays one within this of the approach bearing, timed on its straight distance to the strip if its track misses it: one sample a few degrees off on short final must not drop a live alert.

minGroundSpeedKts.description: Slower than this and an airborne mobile is not flying an approach.

maxAglFt.description: Higher than this above the field and a mobile is not on an approach yet. A position that reports no height above ground reads its true altitude less the runway's threshold elevation.

countdownS.description: The Impending Arrival Window rows, seconds from the landing threshold, largest first and strictly descending. An approach beyond the first row plus fifteen seconds is not listed.

countdownLvpS.description: The rows while low visibility procedures are in force.

stageOneS.description: An arrival this many seconds or less from the landing threshold of a strip with an occupant is a Stage One for both. 30 is the EUROCONTROL-SPEC-171 SAFE-280 and SPEC-202 RMCA-070 example, and Edinburgh's figure. Also the window in which an arrival to a closed runway is alerted.

stageTwoS.description: An arrival this many seconds or less from the landing threshold of a strip with an occupant is a Stage Two for both. 15 is the specification's example. Must be below stageOneS.

stageOneLvpS.description: stageOneS while low visibility procedures are in force. 45 is the specification's low-visibility example; no UK unit's own value is published.

stageTwoLvpS.description: stageTwoS while low visibility procedures are in force. 30 is the specification's low-visibility example. Must be below stageOneLvpS.

oppositeArrivalsS.description: Two arrivals to opposite ends of one strip are alerted when both are this many seconds or less from their thresholds (rules.oppositeArrivals). Absent, the Stage One window in force: stageOneS, stageOneLvpS in low visibility. lookaheadS must reach it.

rules.description: Which scenarios run; each is its own switch so a package imitating another A-SMGCS takes a subset.

occupants.description: Two or more mobiles on one strip: departure, line-up, crossing and opposite direction. Stage One, or Stage Two for a mobile faster than stageTwoSpeedKts and closing on another and for the one it closes on.

arrivalVsOccupant.description: An approaching arrival against a mobile on the strip, through the two windows.

closedRunway.description: Any mobile on a runway the controller closed (.dev rimcas-close), or an arrival to it within stageOneS, is alerted at its stages.closedRunwayOccupant and stages.closedRunwayApproach stage.

oppositeDirection.description: Two moving occupants head-on along one strip are alerted with their own reason, raised before the general two-on-the-runway rule.

restrictedArea.description: A mobile inside a zone tagged strip.restrictedZoneTag is alerted at stages.restrictedArea.

oppositeArrivals.description: Two arrivals to opposite ends of one strip, both within stageOneS of their thresholds, are alerted at stages.oppositeArrivals (EUROCONTROL-SPEC-171 SAFE-250, SPEC-202 RMCA-050).

predictedEntry.description: A mobile on the ground moving at movingKts or more, outside the strip, whose track carries it inside within occupancy.entryLookaheadS, is alerted with every arrival within stageOneS at stages.predictedEntry (SPEC-171 SAFE-260, SPEC-202 RMCA-060). Departures are not yet a class of their own, so only arrivals are judged against it.

stages.description: The stage each scenario and case raises: stageOne (INFORMATION, a caution) or stageTwo (ALARM). EUROCONTROL-SPEC-171 and SPEC-202 leave stage assignment local; every default is SPEC-202's, which differs from the old fixed stages only for an arrival to a closed runway.

occupants.description: Two on one strip, not closing fast.

occupantsClosing.description: Two on one strip, one faster than stageTwoSpeedKts closing on the other.

arrivalApproaching.description: An arrival within stageOneS of the threshold of a strip with an occupant.

arrivalImminent.description: An arrival within stageTwoS of the threshold of a strip with an occupant.

closedRunwayOccupant.description: A mobile on a closed runway (SPEC-202 CMAC-060: ALARM when on it).

closedRunwayApproach.description: An arrival within stageOneS of a closed runway's threshold (SPEC-202 CMAC-060: INFORMATION while foreseen).

oppositeDirection.description: Two moving occupants head-on along one strip.

restrictedArea.description: A mobile inside a restricted area (SPEC-202 CMAC-120: ALARM when in it).

oppositeArrivals.description: Two arrivals to opposite ends of one strip, both inside stageOneS (SESAR SOL02: ALARM).

predictedEntry.description: A mobile predicted into the strip while an arrival is inside stageOneS, and that arrival: INFORMATION before it enters, after which the occupant rules take over.

stageTwoSpeedKts.description: vSMR's rule: an occupant faster than this and closing on another occupant is a Stage Two; slower is a Stage One.

runways.description: What each runway is monitored for, keyed "EGLL 09L/27R" or "EGLL/09L" (either designator names the pair). A runway with no entry gets unlistedRunways. Both flags off and the runway is not monitored at all.

arrivals.description: Predict arrivals to this runway and run the arrival scenarios.

occupancy.description: Track who is on this runway and run the occupancy scenarios.

unlistedRunways.description: What an active runway with no runways entry gets: monitored for everything, or ignored.

approachFunnel.description: AFDAS, the approach path monitor of the EUROCONTROL APM guidelines (G162 Part III), evaluated on the client. An airborne track qualifies on final to a monitored runway end inside the lateral area within onFinalTrackDeg of the course, and from then on is alerted below the lower slope (under the joining altitude), above the upper slope if authored, and laterally, each raised after confirmCycles new reports as one alert naming the side (LO before L or R before HI). A plan's destination and arrival runway, where it has them, are the only ones it is judged against. It judges the QNH altitude: the aircraft's pressure altitude on the QNH of the nearest airport METAR the client holds, else its true altitude. A net of its own: absent means off even with runwayMonitoring authored. The vertical axes need a threshold elevation, which open-navdata.db carries for most but not all runways; an end without one is judged on the lateral axis alone and .dev afdas-info names it.

enabled.description: False stops the funnel evaluating. Use safetyNets.show.afdas instead to keep it evaluating and hide it on this system.

fromNm.description: Nearest distance from the touchdown point that is monitored; inside it the aircraft is landing and the band is within the surveillance's own error (EUROCONTROL G162 MINDISTANCE 2).

toNm.description: Furthest distance from the touchdown point that is monitored, the extent of the lateral area too. Must exceed fromNm. 10 is the NOVA 9000 AFDAS range.

glidepathDeg.description: Nominal glidepath, the path the explainer reports heights against; it must lie between lowerSlopeDeg and upperSlopeDeg. Raise it per end for a steep approach, with the slopes.

lowerSlopeDeg.description: Below this angle up from the touchdown point, and under joiningAltitudeFt, a monitored aircraft is low (G162 LOWERSLOPE 2).

upperSlopeDeg.description: Above this angle up from the touchdown point a monitored aircraft is high, when alertAbove is on (G162 UPPERSLOPE 4).

joiningAltitudeFt.description: The altitude aircraft join the glidepath level at: at or above it nothing is low, so a volume can reach past the point where the lower slope meets the joining level. Absent, the lower slope is the floor all the way out (G162 JOININGHEIGHT).

lateralStartNm.description: Half width of the lateral area at the touchdown point, widening by lateralSlopeDeg each side along the course.

lateralSlopeDeg.description: Half angle the lateral area widens by each side of the course. 20 is half of G162's 40 degree HORIZONTALANGLE wedge. It and lateralStartNm cannot both be 0.

onFinalTrackDeg.description: A track inside the lateral area within this of the course qualifies on final and is monitored from then on; a lateral alert held by trackDeviationDeg clears at this or less. TopSky's 20.

trackDeviationDeg.description: A monitored track more than this off the course raises a lateral alert, held while it stays more than onFinalTrackDeg off. Must exceed onFinalTrackDeg. TopSky's 30.

missedApproachFpm.description: A monitored aircraft climbing faster than this is going around: monitoring stops and its alert goes, until it qualifies again. TopSky's 500.

overflightAltitudeFt.description: At or above this altitude an aircraft is overflying and not monitored. Absent, no altitude stops monitoring.

alertBelow.description: Alert a monitored aircraft below the lower slope (G162 ActivateBelowGlideSlope).

alertAbove.description: Alert a monitored aircraft above the upper slope (G162 ActivateAboveGlideSlope). Off by default: many systems alert below the path only.

alertLateral.description: Alert a monitored aircraft that leaves the lateral area, or turns more than trackDeviationDeg off the course (G162 ActivateHorizontalDeviation). The alert on leaving the area stays until it climbs away or leaves the range.

confirmCycles.description: Distinct position reports outside the funnel before it raises; a sweep that sees no new report does not count, so one legacy report seen on several sweeps is one. Coming back inside clears at once.

ends.description: Per runway END, keyed "EGLC/27": its own approach volume, its final approach course and its touchdown point. Anything the entry does not name is the section's value.

enabled.description: False takes this end out of the net: EUROCONTROL APM-14's inhibition for a runway.

fromNm.description: Nearest distance from the touchdown point that is monitored; inside it the aircraft is landing and the band is within the surveillance's own error (EUROCONTROL G162 MINDISTANCE 2).

toNm.description: Furthest distance from the touchdown point that is monitored, the extent of the lateral area too. Must exceed fromNm. 10 is the NOVA 9000 AFDAS range.

glidepathDeg.description: Nominal glidepath, the path the explainer reports heights against; it must lie between lowerSlopeDeg and upperSlopeDeg. Raise it per end for a steep approach, with the slopes.

lowerSlopeDeg.description: Below this angle up from the touchdown point, and under joiningAltitudeFt, a monitored aircraft is low (G162 LOWERSLOPE 2).

upperSlopeDeg.description: Above this angle up from the touchdown point a monitored aircraft is high, when alertAbove is on (G162 UPPERSLOPE 4).

joiningAltitudeFt.description: The altitude aircraft join the glidepath level at: at or above it nothing is low, so a volume can reach past the point where the lower slope meets the joining level. Absent, the lower slope is the floor all the way out (G162 JOININGHEIGHT).

lateralStartNm.description: Half width of the lateral area at the touchdown point, widening by lateralSlopeDeg each side along the course.

lateralSlopeDeg.description: Half angle the lateral area widens by each side of the course. 20 is half of G162's 40 degree HORIZONTALANGLE wedge. It and lateralStartNm cannot both be 0.

courseDeg.description: The final approach course, degrees true, where it is not the runway's own bearing (an offset localiser or a published offset course). Absent, the runway's bearing from the navdata.

touchdownM.description: Metres the touchdown point lies past the landing threshold, along the runway; the path and the distances start there. Absent, 0: the threshold.

safetyNets.description: The alert board every safety net wears, all of them the client's (BUST, CLAM, RIMCAS, RAM, AIW, AFDAS, MSAW, STCA, TCT, the emergency squawk; MTCD is planned), merged into one ordered set per aircraft and read through alertKind, alertSeverity, alertText, alertOther, alertCount, alertAcknowledged, alertsMuted and the twelve per-kind severities. Unlike the other sections an absent one is the full default rather than off: the board shows only what a label, list or target already asks for, so a package that binds none of those keys sees nothing either way. BUST and CLAM are client nets that take their numbers from safetyNets.bust and safetyNets.clam here, each the server's tuned defaults when absent.

show.description: Hides a kind on this system. An unlisted kind is shown, so name only what this system has no use for: a tower hides mtcd and tct, an area system hides rimcas and afdas. Hiding filters the board and never stops the net evaluating; .dev alert-info says which kinds are hidden.

sounds.description: Sound ids in the package's sounds folder, played once when an aircraft's highest alert escalates. Absent plays nothing, which is what a package that authors no sounds gets. Each id is the name of a file in the package's sounds folder without its extension (stca is sounds/stca.wav, else sounds/stca.mp3), never a path. An id with no file is logged as a warning and plays nothing.

info.description: Played when the highest alert reaches info severity (MTCD, TCT).

warning.description: Played when it reaches warning severity (CLAM, RAM, AIW, RIMCAS Stage One).

alert.description: Played when it reaches alert severity (MSAW, BUST, RIMCAS Stage Two, an emergency squawk).

alertRepeatS.description: Seconds between repeats of the alert sound while any unacknowledged alert-severity alert stands anywhere. 0 plays once per escalation, which is the default; NOVA keeps sounding, vSMR sounded once.

newEntryMinSeverity.description: The lowest severity at which a new alert is a new alarm: one raised on an aircraft already alerting, under its highest alert, plays its own sound, asks again for an acknowledgement given to the alert above it, and ends a session mute. alert by default, the surface specifications' new ALARM.

perKind.description: Replaces the severity sound for one kind, so MSAW can have its own tone.

mute.description: What the muteAlerts click action does. It silences the sounds of the kinds that are mutable (kinds.<kind>.mutable: every kind but emergency and rimcas unless authored), a new alert-severity alert anywhere ends it and plays, the end of the FSD session ends it, and it lapses by itself after expiresS. The colour, the blink and alertsMuted are the controller's cue that sound is off.

expiresS.description: Seconds a mute lasts before sound returns by itself. 0 never lapses. Five minutes by default: a mute quietens one nuisance episode and must not outlive it.

inhibit.description: What the inhibitAlerts click action does. It switches this client's nets off for one aircraft (kinds.<kind>.inhibitable) until the controller lifts it, the aircraft goes, its pilot changes or the FSD session ends, and after expiresS when one is authored. alertsInhibited marks the aircraft and alertOtherInhibited the other aircraft of an alert. For STCA it is one of the two flags that silence a pair.

expiresS.description: Seconds an inhibit lasts before it lapses by itself. 0, the default, never lapses, so an inhibit stays until it is lifted. An inhibitor never reset after use is a fault-tree cause in the EUROCONTROL STCA guidance.

acknowledge.description: What the acknowledgeAlert click action does. The colour always stays: acknowledging says the controller has seen the alert, not that it has gone, and a change of kind or severity re-arms it by itself. A pairwise alert also re-arms for good when the other aircraft changes or its predicted separation closes (rearmOnCpaDecreaseNm).

silencesSound.description: An acknowledged alert stops driving sounds.alertRepeatS.

expiresS.description: Seconds an acknowledgement lasts before the alert re-arms. 0 never lapses.

rearmOnCpaDecreaseNm.description: Nautical miles a pairwise alert's predicted closest lateral distance must shrink after the click before the acknowledgement is spent, TopSky's de-acknowledge on a separation decrease: an STCA acknowledged at 2.8 NM that closes to 1.8 NM sounds and asks again, and opening back out does not re-acknowledge it. 0 turns the rule off; a new other aircraft re-arms either way. STCA and TCT carry a predicted distance; any other pairwise alert keeps the kind-and-severity rule.

pairs.description: What acknowledging one aircraft of a pairwise alert (STCA, TCT) does to the other. both acknowledges the same alert on the other aircraft too, while it is that aircraft's highest, so the partner stops blinking and repeating with it; one leaves the other end to be acknowledged on its own.

priority.description: Which kind alertKind and alertText report when several stand on one aircraft, highest first. Kinds left out follow the listed ones in the default order, so a partial list cannot hide one, and an emergency left out ranks above every listed kind. Severity breaks a tie within a kind, then the age of the alert. Use the per-kind keys instead where a system wants each net placed by hand.

emergencySquawk.description: Raises an alert-severity Emergency on any aircraft squawking an emergency code (emergencyCodes: 7500, 7600 and 7700 unless the package adds one), with the code's words and the code as alertText. A code set while the transponder is on standby, or on a track only a primary radar sees, raises nothing. Client-side and needs no server.

emergencyCodes.description: Emergency codes by four-digit code, on top of 7500 HIJACK, 7600 RADIO FAILURE and 7700 EMERGENCY: the codes the emergency squawk net raises and the filter bypass reads. A code listed here is added, one of the three is reworded; none is taken away. The UK adds 7400 LST LNK.

text.description: What alertText shows before the code: LST LNK reads LST LNK 7400.

bypassFilters.description: An alerted track is drawn whatever the view's filters say, which is TopSky's rule and the one safety matter in the presentation: an aircraft in conflict below the lower altitude filter is otherwise invisible. On by default, and it beats every filter including GND, PRIM and VFR, not just the altitude band. An emergency code (safetyNets.emergencyCodes) always bypasses, whether or not this is on and whether or not emergencySquawk raised a net, unless the transponder is on standby or only a primary radar sees the track. .dev alert-info says when the bypass is what put the aircraft on screen.

enabled.description: False lets the view filters hide an alerted track, but never one squawking an emergency code. Turn it off knowing what that costs.

minSeverity.description: The lowest severity that lifts a track out of the filters. warning covers RAM, AIW and RIMCAS Stage One; alert restricts it to STCA, MSAW, BUST, RIMCAS Stage Two and the emergency squawk; info includes the planning nets, which is usually too much.

kinds.description: The kinds whose alerts lift a track out of the filters, each at or above minSeverity. Absent, or empty, is every kind. Whichever kinds are named, a pairwise alert of a named kind (STCA, TCT) lifts both of its aircraft at any severity, so a TCT in its warning band and the other aircraft of a conflict are never left to the filters. TopSky lifts emergency, stca, msaw, afdas, apw, aiw and tct, and never clam, ram or mtcd: the safety nets, not the monitoring aids. An emergency code bypasses whatever this says.

alertVector.description: The prediction line an alerted airborne aircraft is forced to carry, TopSky's one-minute line. It is drawn only where the view's profile draws no speed vector at all, in the time style, in the colour the drawn target variant's speedVectorColor gives; a profile already showing a vector keeps its own length. On by default. A variant keyed on alertSeverity is how the symbol, the history dots and this line change colour; nothing here is a colour.

enabled.description: False leaves an alerted aircraft with the profile's own vector, or none.

minutes.description: Whole minutes of track, one tick per minute as the profile's time vector is drawn. To draw none, set enabled false.

minSeverity.description: The lowest severity of the aircraft's TOP alert that forces the line. warning covers RAM, AIW and RIMCAS Stage One; alert restricts it to STCA, MSAW, BUST, RIMCAS Stage Two and the emergency squawk. A ground aircraft never draws a vector, whatever its alert.

exclude.description: Aircraft the client-side nets leave out: TCT, RAM, AIW, MSAW, AFDAS, BUST and CLAM skip them at their eligibility stage, and STCA keeps them in its pair loop and silences a pair only when both aircraft are excluded or inhibited. An aircraft is excluded when a callsign pattern matches, or a squawk prefix matches, or the when condition holds; any one is enough. The duplicate-code detector in Correlation stops calling a code listed in squawks duplicated (TopSky's Airspace_No_DUPE_Codes); it reads squawks alone, never callsigns or when. The emergency squawk net and RIMCAS are never excluded. A controller's per-aircraft twin of this is the inhibitAlerts click action. Note that excluding the conspicuity codes silences AIW on exactly the traffic AIW exists to watch, the untracked VFR under a TMA, so list them only when that is what the vAcc wants.

callsigns.description: Callsign patterns, TopSky's wildcard: * stands for any run of characters, anywhere, and the match is whole and case insensitive ("GLID*", "*TEST", "BAW123"). A bare "*" is refused, because it would take every aircraft out of every net.

squawks.description: Octal SSR code prefixes, TopSky's form: "20" is 2000 to 2077, "7000" is that code alone. One to four octal digits; anything else is a load error naming the entry.

when.description: Exclude by rule: every aircraft this condition holds for is excluded, on top of callsigns and squawks. Written and read exactly as an applyWhen: a "$name" of the package's systems/expressions file, one [operator, key, value] comparison, or an AND / OR / NOT group, over any aircraft key (the military rule the tags already use, ["contains", "zoneTags", "danger"], a flight rule). Absent or empty excludes nobody. It is read as each net sweeps, against the track as the screen last drew it. A condition that cannot be read, one naming an expression that does not exist and one whose evaluation fails exclude nobody; each is logged once and listed by .dev package-check. .dev alert-info says when it is what excluded an aircraft.

ram.description: Route adherence monitoring, evaluated on the client against the route expansion the server landed on the flight plan, so the numbers are the package's. It measures cross-track distance to the leg the aircraft is flying and raises a warning-severity Ram with the distance as alertText. The server is still the only route expander, so with no server there is no expansion and the net is silent rather than clean; .dev ram-info says which of the two it is. Absent is every default below, as an absent safetyNets section is.

enabled.description: False stops the net evaluating at all. Use safetyNets.show.ram instead to keep it evaluating and hide it on this system.

triggerNm.description: Cross-track distance from the leg's centreline that raises the net, TopSky's number. Must be at least clearNm.

clearNm.description: Cross-track distance the aircraft must come back inside for the net to clear. Below triggerNm on purpose: the band between the two is the hysteresis that stops an aircraft riding the trigger flapping every cycle.

confirmCycles.description: New position reports in a row beyond triggerNm before the net raises; a check that sees no new report counts nothing. At one report every 5 seconds the default raises 5 to 10 seconds after the deviation crosses the trigger. Clearing needs no confirmation.

cadenceS.description: Seconds between checks. The net rides the 2 Hz position batch and skips the batches inside this window; the default checks every report a pilot client sends every 5 seconds, as the route deviation check compares on each track update.

maxDeviationNm.description: Beyond this the net says nothing: the flight is not flying that route at all and a permanent alert on it is noise. Must exceed triggerNm.

directInhibitS.description: How long an assigned direct-to the server has not folded into the expansion yet inhibits the net, because the legs still describe the old path. The bound is what stops a direct the server never folds leaving the net silent on that aircraft for the session.

inhibitNearDepartureNm.description: Within this distance of the flight plan's departure airport the net says nothing: departures are vectored off the filed route whether or not the controller keyed the heading. Measured from the airport, never from the route's first point, which a folded direct-to moves to its fix; an airport the client's navdata does not place gets no inhibit. TopSky's 30 NM. 0 turns the inhibit off.

inhibitNearDestinationNm.description: Within this distance of the route's last point, the destination, the net says nothing, for the same reason on arrival. TopSky's 30 NM. 0 turns the inhibit off.

scope.description: Whose traffic the net judges. ownedOrConcerned, the default, is this controller's own and the traffic its attention tiers name (concerned, notified, an incoming or outgoing transfer, an intruder), as the sector controlling a flight is warned; another controller's flight is not judged, sounded or lifted through the view filters. allVisible judges every aircraft the client holds.

flightRules.description: Which flights the net judges, TopSky's VFR switch, on the vocabulary bust and clam share. ifr, the default, leaves out a flight that filed VFR and one that filed no rule, which bust and clam judge as IFR: neither has a route to hold to, and EuroScope never raises RAM for a VFR plan. vfr judges filed VFR flights alone. all judges every flight with a route.

uncontrolled.description: Whether an uncontrolled flight is judged: a flight that filed VFR and no controller tracks. An IFR flight, and an unfiled one where flightRules admits it, is judged tracked or not, so this matters only where flightRules admits VFR. On by default for RAM, as TopSky's RAM_Uncontrolled.

waypointRadiusNm.description: Within this distance of either end of the leg being flown, where the route turns there by waypointMinTurnDeg or more, the net does not raise: an aircraft anticipating a fly-by turn cuts inside the corner. The route's first and last points have no leg beyond them and always count as a turn. It stops a raise only and never clears a standing alert. TopSky's Wpt_Radius, 5 NM. 0 turns it off.

waypointMinTurnDeg.description: The smallest change of course at a leg end that counts as a turn for waypointRadiusNm. TopSky's Wpt_MinTurn, 10 degrees.

directTrackErrorDeg.description: On a direct-to the server has folded into the expansion, the turn onto it is done once the track is within this of the bearing to the fix, and the direct is measured from there; until then, for at most 120 s from the fold, the net does not raise. An aircraft that was on track to the fix holds the passed-fix guard until it is back within clearNm of the route after the fix. TopSky's DCT_MaxTrkError, 5 degrees.

msaw.description: Minimum safe altitude warning, evaluated on the client against the package's own datasets/msaw.geojson. Unlike stca this net is ON wherever that file exists: its figures are the vAcc's own published surface rather than a tuning nobody has done, so absent means every default below. WITH NO SURFACE THE NET IS SILENT RATHER THAN CLEAN, and .dev msaw-info says which of the two it is instead of reporting every aircraft above a minimum. Raises an alert-severity Msaw with the minimum as alertText, and publishes the minimum under each aircraft as the msaFt expression whether or not it alerts. It judges the altitude an altimeter set to QNH reads, as TopSky and EUROCONTROL's MSAW reference do: the pressure altitude corrected by the QNH of the nearest airport METAR within 100 NM, the frame a cleared altitude is flown in; with no such METAR, or a pilot client that relays no pressure difference, the true altitude. An approach-clearance inhibit (TopSky's MSAW_AppInhibit) is authored as safetyNets.kinds.msaw.exclude.when over clearedFlightLevel, 2 for a visual approach and 1 for an ILS, never under safetyNets.exclude, which would take the approach out of AFDAS as well.

enabled.description: False stops the net evaluating at all. Use safetyNets.show.msaw instead to keep it evaluating and hide it on this system.

bufferFt.description: The trigger is the minimum LESS this, for an IFR flight. A raised alert clears at the minimum plus clearFt, so an aircraft cruising at exactly the minimum neither raises nor, once raised, flaps. The default 300 is TopSky's stock MSAW_Buffer_IFR and inside the several hundred feet EUROCONTROL's MSAW guidance allows below a minimum; the UK authors its own 100.

lookaheadS.description: How far ahead the path is predicted, seconds; 0, the default, is no prediction, as TopSky. Authored, the aircraft is stepped every predictionStepS along its ground track at its current vertical rate, a climb, level flight and a descent alike, and every step is judged against the minimum at its own point; a step in an msaFt 0 area is skipped and the next one judged. No cleared level caps or replaces the predicted altitude. A straight-line descent goes through the ground inside 2 NM of any runway, so a lookahead wants the surface to carry funnels along every final.

predictionStepS.description: Seconds between the predicted points along the path when lookaheadS is authored, the last point at lookaheadS. Five is one report interval: 0.4 NM at 300 kt, inside the half to one NM cells EUROCONTROL's MSAW guidance sizes a terrain grid by, so a cell that size is not stepped over below 360 kt; the guidance finds 1 s steps feasible for a finer surface, which is the least the client takes.

cadenceS.description: Seconds between evaluations inside the 2 Hz sweep. Five is how often a pilot client sends a position; an evaluation that sees no new report counts for nothing in the confirmation.

confirmCycles.description: Hits among the last cycleCount evaluations with a new report that confirm a PREDICTED infringement, EUROCONTROL's TerrainConflictCount (2 or 3 advised); a miss in between does not reset the count. An aircraft already below the trigger, or predicted below it within imminentS, raises at once.

clearFt.description: Height above the minimum at which a raised alert clears, held for one more new report so a single report at the minimum does not end it. 0, the default, clears at the minimum, as BUST and CLAM take their own clearFt; with bufferFt it makes the band in which a raised alert holds and a clear track stays clear.

cycleCount.description: How many of the latest evaluations with a new report confirmCycles is counted over, EUROCONTROL's TerrainCycleCount (4 or 5 advised). It may not be less than confirmCycles.

imminentS.description: A predicted infringement this many seconds ahead or sooner raises at once, with no confirmation, EUROCONTROL's TerrainImminentTime. 0, the default, makes only an actual infringement imminent; it matters only with a lookahead.

flightRules.description: Which flights the net watches. An unfiled rule satisfies neither ifr nor vfr, so it is out of both. Absent is ifr: a VFR flight is not watched unless the system authors all.

uncontrolled.description: Whether a VFR flight no controller holds is judged. Off, as TopSky's MSAW_Uncontrolled: the surface is a controller's vectoring minimum, and a VFR flight under the TMA is below it all day. An IFR flight, and an unfiled one under flightRules all, is judged whether or not anyone tracks it.

bufferVfrFt.description: bufferFt for VFR flights, TopSky's MSAW_Buffer_VFR.

soundScope.description: Who HEARS an MSAW alert, on STCA's vocabulary. allVisible, the default, sounds every one, as before. ownedOrConcerned sounds only an aircraft this controller owns or its attention tiers name, because EUROCONTROL's MSAW hazard assessment found an alert addressed to every position disturbs the room; the alert still shows, colours and lists everywhere, and only the sound is held. safetyNets.kinds.msaw.sound still overrides it.

stca.description: Short term conflict alert, evaluated on the client: a predicted loss of separation between two aircraft inside the lookahead, raised as an alert-severity Stca naming the other aircraft in alertOther. The largest net here, and the one where a naive implementation is worse than none, so unlike every other safetyNets key it is OFF until this section is authored: it wants regions tuned to the airspace first. Its whole budget goes on nuisance suppression rather than sensor noise, because positions here come from the pilot client and are exact. .dev stca-info prints every pair the last cycle looked at and why each was rejected.

enabled.description: False stops the net evaluating. Use safetyNets.show.stca instead to keep it evaluating and hide it on this system.

lookaheadS.description: How far ahead a conflict is predicted. Absent is 120, 30 seconds past the default warningS, so a conflict's confirmation has built by the time it comes inside warningS and it alerts on the first report there; a hit beyond warningS counts toward the confirmation but never alerts. Longer sees more and cries wolf more, and TCT is the five minute tool.

sampleS.description: Step of the sampled paths: round a turn, and the straight line when either track levels off inside the window, may leave its level for its cleared level, or has a turn rate that cannot be known. Two straight tracks otherwise use a closed form and never sample.

levelOffAtCfl.description: Assume an aircraft stops climbing or descending at its cleared level, which is the largest single nuisance reduction available. Its blind spot is the aircraft that does not stop, so the net carries its own per-aircraft guard: a track that has transited its cleared level by more than 300 ft and is still going keeps the observed rate whatever this says. False turns the assumption off for every aircraft; nothing can pin it on past the guard.

warningS.description: A confirmed conflict alerts once its predicted loss of separation is no more than this many seconds away, G159's warning time (TopSky 90 upper, 80 lower). Absent is 90, or lookaheadS where that is shorter; more than lookaheadS is refused.

lowerWarningS.description: The warning time at or below upperLateralAboveFt, TopSky's lower band (STCA_WarningTime_L, 80 against 90 above). Absent is warningS, one time for every band, which is what a system authoring neither has always had. A pair takes the upper band's time when either aircraft is above upperLateralAboveFt.

imminentS.description: A conflict whose loss is no more than this many seconds away alerts on the cycle it is first seen, without waiting for conflictCount (G159's imminent time; TopSky 50). A pair already inside its minima is imminent. Absent is 50, or warningS where that is shorter; more than warningS is refused.

conflictCount.description: How many of the last cycleCount checks must find the conflict before it alerts (G159's M of N; TopSky 2). Only a check that sees a new position report from either aircraft counts: the sweep is 2 Hz and many pilot clients report every five seconds, so one report seen on successive sweeps is one sample. Must not exceed cycleCount.

cycleCount.description: How many of the most recent counting checks conflictCount is judged over (G159's N; TopSky 4).

clearS.description: Seconds a raised pair must stay clear before it is dropped, so a single missed position report does not flash the alert off and on.

scope.description: Who is shown a pair. ownedOrConcerned raises when at least one of the two is ours by the attention tiers the containment sweep already computes, which is what keeps an ACC controller from seeing constant conflicts between aircraft nobody is working. allVisible iterates everything and costs about ten times as many pair tests.

soundScope.description: Who HEARS a pair, TopSky's separate STCA alert sound scope. Absent is the same as scope, and it can only narrow it: a pair outside scope never reaches the alert board at all, so allVisible here with ownedOrConcerned above is refused as silencing nothing. A pair outside the sound scope still shows, still colours and still lands in the alert list; only the sound is held.

turnRateThresholdDegS.description: At or above this a track with a known turn rate is turning, and its pairs are also predicted round the turn (turning). A track whose rate cannot be known at all is predicted straight, sampled, with its lateral minimum widened.

turning.description: The turning prediction, G159's turning filter. Every pair is always judged on the straight line; a pair with a turning track is ALSO judged round the turn, for timeS and on lateralNm, and a conflict on either path alerts. Absent is on at the defaults.

timeS.description: How long the turn is predicted (G159 70 to 90 s, TopSky's Turn_React 70). Absent is 70, or lookaheadS where that is shorter; more than lookaheadS is refused.

lateralNm.description: The lateral minimum round the turn (G159 1.5 to 2.5 nm in a TMA, 3.0 to 4.0 en route; TopSky 2 and 3). It never widens the pair's own minimum. Absent is the pair's own minimum.

defaultRegion.description: The minima anywhere no region rule matches on that axis. The defaults are TopSky's thresholds (G159 Part 3 section 3.6: somewhat less than the separation standard), so with no buffer a pair exactly on a standard reads clear.

upperLateralNm.description: Above upperLateralAboveFt (TopSky STCA_LinPred_Sep_Lat_U). Only the default region takes it; a region rule selects its band with aboveFl.

vertical2000Ft.description: G159's [2000] vertical value, taken in place of verticalFt by a pair rvsm puts on the 2000 ft standard.

rvsm.description: G159's pair rule for the [2000] vertical value: a pair takes vertical2000Ft when both aircraft are above upperFl, or both are above lowerFl and either is not RVSM approved, and verticalFt otherwise. Approval is read from the filed equipment: W in ICAO item 10a, or the FAA suffixes H, W, Z and L. Absent is on at the defaults.

lowerFl.description: Strictly above this a non-RVSM aircraft is on the 2000 ft standard (G159's LowerSeparationFlightLevel). 285 puts FL290 above it. Must be below upperFl.

upperFl.description: Strictly above this every pair is on the 2000 ft standard (G159's UpperSeparationFlightLevel, the top of RVSM airspace). 415 starts at FL420.

unknownApproved.description: Whether an aircraft whose filed equipment says nothing about RVSM (no plan, an unparsed type field) counts as approved. False is G159's rule, unknown counted not approved; true is a stated VATSIM adaptation for blank or wrong equipment fields.

regions.description: Per-airspace minima. A rule's lateralNm and verticals also SCALE every other value of the net for its tracks, as TopSky's STCA areas do: current proximity, fast diverging and the turning lateral by the rule's lateral over the default region's value for the band (2.75 nm in a TMA is 0.61 of the 4.5 nm upper band), the vertical values likewise, and a pair takes the larger scale of its two aircraft. A Volume carries no tags, so a rule selects on sector id globs, a zones.geojson tag, an altitude band, or any combination; every selector it names must hold. A rule OVERRIDES the default on the axes it names and leaves the others alone, and where several rules match one track the most conservative of each axis wins. Two aircraft in different regions take the most conservative of the two, so a tighter TMA region can never silence a conflict the en-route region beside it would have raised.

sectorIds.description: Sector id globs, for example EGTT_LTC*. A trailing star is the only wildcard. This is the one selector that costs a volume resolve per track; a package using only zoneTag and aboveFl pays nothing.

zoneTag.description: A tag on a zones.geojson polygon the package draws for the purpose.

aboveFl.description: Applies at or above this flight level, for example 410 for the 2000 ft band.

vertical2000Ft.description: The [2000] vertical value in this region; see rvsm.

warningS.description: The warning time in this region, in either band, as a TopSky STCA_AREA's STCA_ALERT_TIMES. From imminentS to lookaheadS. A pair takes the longer of its two aircraft's times, each the region's where one names it, else its band's.

buffers.description: An uncertainty allowance added on top of the minima and growing with time. None by default, because the default minima are already TopSky's thresholds inside the standard; a system authoring the standard itself as its minima would need one, and a buffer is why an aircraft levelling off exactly on a minimum reads as a conflict.

exclusionZoneTag.description: A zone tag inside which every pair of a track is still judged and kept silent, for airspace where converging traffic is the procedure: the confirmation runs on, so a pair leaving it into a conflict alerts on its first sweep outside. Whole tags only, so no spaces.

finalApproach.description: The final-approach corridor, generated behind EVERY monitored landing end from the runway ends runway monitoring already resolves, so authoring an empty object gets the behaviour at every airport in the package with nothing drawn. Inside a corridor two aircraft landing in trail on the course, where the wake rule allows it (the nearer no heavy, super or B757, the further the same category or heavier), are judged against lateralNm instead of the region's own minimum; every other pair in there keeps the region's minimum. Nothing is silenced: an approach that should raise nothing is an authored exclusion zone. ABSENT IS OFF, because a corridor lowers the minimum. IT NEEDS policy.json runwayMonitoring: the geometry comes from those strips, so a system authoring this and no runway monitoring generates nothing, which .dev stca-info says in those words.

enabled.description: False keeps the section as documentation without generating anything.

rangeNm.description: How far back from the threshold the corridor runs.

xteNm.description: Half width either side of the extended centreline.

lateralNm.description: The lateral minimum for a wake-compatible pair in trail on one final, on the prediction and on current proximity, which replaces the region's where it is smaller. It never widens one: a corridor reduces separation on final, it does not tighten the net.

courseToleranceDeg.description: How far off the approach course a track may be and still count as flying it. A track crossing the corridor is in it but not on the course, so it keeps the region's minimum.

parallel.description: Runway pairs worked at the same time. The package names them because nothing in the data says which runways an aerodrome operates simultaneously. A pair applies only while the aerodrome's runway selection has BOTH runways active for arrivals. One aircraft in each normal operating zone, each landing at the aerodrome (on that zone's runway when it filed one), each tracking within courseToleranceDeg of its own approach course and the two at least minSepNm apart, is the operation working rather than a conflict: the pair is still judged and kept silent, so one leaving its zone into a conflict alerts at once. A pair naming a runway no monitored strip carries, or one not landing on both, is reported by .dev stca-info rather than silently matching nothing.

icao.description: The aerodrome both runways belong to.

left.description: One runway's landing designator, as the strip carries it.

right.description: The other one. Naming the same runway twice is a load error.

rangeNm.description: How far back each operating zone runs from its threshold.

nozNm.description: Half width of each operating zone either side of its centreline.

departure.description: True for a simultaneous DEPARTURE pair rather than an approach pair.

leftCourseT.description: Approach course in degrees true where it differs from the runway's own bearing.

rightCourseT.description: The same for the other runway.

leftApproachAltFt.description: The level assumed for this runway when the clearance is "cleared for approach" rather than a number, which is the level-off model's missing case on final.

rightApproachAltFt.description: The same for the other runway.

ntzZoneTag.description: A zones.geojson tag for the no transgression zone between the two. This is the one piece of approach geometry that turns the net ON: a track inside it is exactly what simultaneous operations forbid, so NO generated region may silence a pair while either aircraft is in there.

minSepNm.description: Two aircraft closer than this are a conflict whatever zones they are in (TopSky's SOIR MinSep).

courseToleranceDeg.description: How far off its own zone's approach course a track may be and still fly the operation (TopSky's STCA_NOZ_Delta_HDG). The final approach corridor keeps its own finalApproach.courseToleranceDeg.

maxNewAlertsPerCycle.description: How many NEW alerts one cycle may raise, so an event peak cannot produce a wall of them at once. The rest are DEFERRED to the next cycle in order of time to loss, never dropped: a dropped alert is a silent blindness.

floorFt.description: No track below this altitude takes part, TopSky's STCA_Floor: at or below the transition altitude it is an altitude on QNH, above it a pressure altitude. Aerodrome traffic converging on a runway is the procedure, and the final approach corridors and runway monitoring watch it there.

maxTrackAgeS.description: A track whose last position report is older than this takes no part, TopSky's STCA_Max_Track_Age: a frozen position predicts a conflict that is not there.

vfrPairs.description: Whether a pair of two VFR flights alerts, TopSky's STCA_VFR. Off: VFR traffic separates itself.

uncontrolledPairs.description: Whether a pair of two uncontrolled flights alerts, TopSky's STCA_Uncontrolled. Off. An uncontrolled flight is a VFR one nobody tracks; an IFR flight, or one with no plan, counts as controlled, tracked or not.

formationMarker.description: The flight plan remarks marker that names a formation, TopSky's System_FPL_F18_Formation_Text: after a blank (or at the start of the remarks) the marker, then the members joined by '+' up to the next blank, for example FOR/LYNX31+LYNX32 in the leader's plan. Two members of one formation are never paired, as TopSky leaves them out of STCA. A TopSky-only rule: absent or empty is off, and TopSky ships with no marker.

sourceStates.description: The attention states a source may be in, in place of scope; soundScope absent then sounds for every source.

targetStates.description: The attention states the other aircraft of a pair may be in. Absent is every state.

regionOverlap.description: How the regions matching one track combine: mostConservative takes the widest minimum (and the earliest alert time) of every matching region, firstInFile the first matching region that names each setting, as TopSky reads its areas file. With mostConservative a tighter region can never narrow a wider one it sits inside.

upperLateralAboveFt.description: Above this pressure altitude a track takes defaultRegion.upperLateralNm and the upper lateral values of fastDiverging and currentProximity; a pair takes the upper fastDiverging and currentProximity values when either aircraft does (TopSky's STCA_Sep_Lat_SepLevel).

fastDiverging.description: G159's fast-diverging conditions, TopSky's values, judged on the two aircraft as they are now. Laterally: opening at lateralKt or more and at least lateralNm apart (upperLateralNm above upperLateralAboveFt), so the straight-line and current proximity filters find nothing this cycle; the turning prediction still runs. Vertically: diverging at verticalFpm or more and at least verticalFt apart (vertical2000Ft on the 2000 ft standard), so no filter finds anything. A pair already inside its minima and opening fast clears instead of alerting to the end of its window. Absent is on at the defaults.

enabled.description: False switches both tests off.

lateralNm.description: Lateral distance apart at or below upperLateralAboveFt (TopSky STCA_FastDiv_Sep_Lat_L).

verticalFt.description: Vertical distance apart on the 1000 ft standard (STCA_FastDiv_Sep_Vert_L).

vertical2000Ft.description: Vertical distance apart on the 2000 ft standard, which rvsm decides (STCA_FastDiv_Sep_Vert_U).

currentProximity.description: G159's current proximity filter, TopSky's values: a pair closer than lateralNm (upperLateralNm above upperLateralAboveFt) and verticalFt (vertical2000Ft on the 2000 ft standard) now is a hit, confirmed on its own conflictCount of cycleCount reports with no warning time, so a pair close but closing too slowly for the prediction to alert is still raised. Inside one final-approach corridor its lateral is no wider than finalApproach.lateralNm. Absent is on at the defaults.

enabled.description: False switches the filter off.

lateralNm.description: At or below upperLateralAboveFt (TopSky STCA_CurrProx_Sep_Lat_L; G159 2.0 to 2.85 in a TMA).

conflictCount.description: Hits needed of the last cycleCount checks with a new report. Must not exceed cycleCount.

cycleCount.description: How many counting checks conflictCount is judged over.

noCfl.description: The second vertical hypothesis (NETALERT 15's multi-hypothesis): where levelOffAtCfl stops a track at its cleared level inside the lookahead, the pair is judged again as if neither aircraft stops there, on minima no wider than these, and a conflict on either alerts. It catches a bust through the clearance before it happens, which levelOffAtCfl alone alerts only once it has; VATSIM does not guarantee a cleared level. The narrower minima keep it to serious busts with real lateral erosion. Absent is off; an empty object is on at the defaults.

enabled.description: False keeps the section as documentation without judging the second hypothesis.

lateralNm.description: The lateral minimum of the second hypothesis, never wider than the pair's own.

verticalFt.description: The vertical minimum of the second hypothesis, never wider than the pair's own.

cflLeave.description: The Blind Spots study's most efficient barrier (PB5): a level aircraft whose cleared level differs by more than atLevelFt may start towards it any time within leaveLevelS at minFpm to maxFpm, so STCA judges the pair on that band before the crew moves. Off unless authored.

enabled.description: False switches it off.

leaveLevelS.description: Latest the level change may start.

atLevelFt.description: Within this of the cleared level the aircraft is already there.

aiw.description: Airspace infringement warning, evaluated on the client: a correlated track no controller is tracking, inside or about to enter controlled airspace, which is the most common real incident on VATSIM. The sector file carries no airspace class, so controlled airspace is every ACTIVE volume whose sector an online controller works, unless this package draws its own with zones tagged controlledZoneTag, which then replace the volume rule entirely. It raises a warning-severity Aiw naming the airspace. 'Not on frequency' is deliberately not part of the rule: a pilot's tuned frequency is in neither the position stream nor the datafeed, so neither half can evaluate it. Absent is every default below, as an absent safetyNets section is. .dev aiw-info prints the airspace set it used.

enabled.description: False stops the net evaluating at all. Use safetyNets.show.aiw instead to keep it evaluating and hide it on this system.

lookaheadS.description: How far ahead on the current track the net looks for an entry, TopSky's sampling. 0 monitors containment alone, which a system that dislikes predicted calls wants; the lookahead is also what keeps a track skimming a boundary from flapping, because clearing needs no confirmation.

confirmCycles.description: New position reports in a row inside or entering before the net raises; a check that sees no new report counts nothing. At one report every 5 seconds the default raises 5 to 10 seconds after the aircraft is first judged inside or entering. Leaving clears at once.

cadenceS.description: Seconds between evaluations. The net rides the 2 Hz position batch and skips the batches inside this window, so a pilot client reporting less often than this is still counted once per report; the default matches how often a pilot client sends a position.

controlledZoneTag.description: A zone tag in datasets/zones.geojson that marks airspace this net monitors. Authoring even one such zone REPLACES the online-volume rule with the zones alone, which is how a vAcc says precisely which CAS it wants watched. Whole tags only, so no spaces. An empty string turns the override off and leaves the volume rule in force.

flightRules.description: Which flights the net watches, TopSky's AIW_FlightRules. vfr watches VFR and unfiled traffic, which is the UK NODE setup: an IFR flight in controlled airspace is on a clearance by definition.

floorFt.description: No alert below this altitude, TopSky's AIW_Floor (1000 in TopSky): at or below the transition altitude it is an altitude on QNH, above it a pressure altitude. Absent is no floor.

scope.description: Whose airspace is watched, TopSky's AIW_Type. own watches only the volumes this controller, or a position it observes, works; ignored when the package draws controlled zones, which name nobody.

bust.description: Level bust: the aircraft has passed through its cleared level by more than triggerFt. Raises an alert-severity Bust worded with the cleared level, as BUST A060 or BUST FL350. A client net; absent is every default below, the values the server tuned it with, never off.

enabled.description: False stops the net evaluating at all. Use safetyNets.show.bust instead to keep it evaluating and hide it on this system.

triggerFt.description: How far beyond the cleared level, in feet, the aircraft must be before the net raises.

rvsmTriggerFt.description: triggerFt for a cleared level from FL290 to FL410, the RVSM band, where EUROCONTROL's level bust is 200 ft rather than 300. clearFt is held no wider than it there.

clearFt.description: How close to the cleared level, in feet, the aircraft must come back for the net to clear. Must not exceed triggerFt: the band between the two is the hysteresis that stops an aircraft riding the trigger flapping.

confirmCycles.description: Distinct position reports beyond triggerFt before the net raises; an evaluation that sees no new report does not count.

inhibitAfterCflChangeSeconds.description: Seconds after the cleared level changes during which the net does not raise while the track is still level, so a new clearance is not an alert before the crew has reacted. The window ends for that clearance as soon as the track climbs or descends, or drifts away from the new level. It holds off a raise only. A new cleared level clears a standing alert at once only when the aircraft is within clearFt of it or closing on it; otherwise the alert stands, worded with the new level.

scope.description: Whose traffic the net judges. ownedOrConcerned, the default, is this controller's own and the traffic its attention tiers name (concerned, notified, an incoming or outgoing transfer, an intruder), as the sector controlling a flight is warned; another controller's flight is not judged, sounded or lifted through the view filters. allVisible judges every aircraft the client holds.

flightRules.description: Which flights the net judges, TopSky's VFR switch. ifr, the default, leaves out a flight that filed VFR; an unfiled rule counts as IFR here. vfr judges filed VFR flights alone.

uncontrolled.description: Whether an uncontrolled flight is judged: a flight that filed VFR and no controller tracks. An IFR or unfiled flight is judged tracked or not, so this matters only where flightRules admits VFR. Off by default, as TopSky's CLAM_Uncontrolled.

clam.description: Cleared level adherence monitoring: the aircraft is more than triggerFt off its cleared level and not closing on it. Raises a warning-severity Clam worded with the cleared level, as CLAM FL350, and stands down while a bust stands on the same aircraft. A client net; absent is every default below, the values the server tuned it with, never off.

enabled.description: False stops the net evaluating at all. Use safetyNets.show.clam instead to keep it evaluating and hide it on this system.

transitionAltitudeFt.description: The highest cleared level that is an altitude on QNH, one value for the whole system and every net that compares a cleared level: at or below it BUST and CLAM judge the altitude the QNH of the nearest airport METAR the client holds gives the aircraft's pressure altitude (its true altitude when no METAR within 100 NM has one, or its pilot client relays no pressure altitude, which is logged once) and word the level A060, above it its pressure altitude and FL350. A cleared level carries no altitude or flight level marker on the wire, so this alone decides which it is.

tct.description: Tactical controller tool, evaluated on the client: TopSky's TCT, a five minute conflict probe built on STCA's pipeline. Laterally it follows an assigned heading after a modelled turn (then the ground track once the turn is complete), else the expanded route while the aircraft conforms to it, else the present ground track; vertically a band of rates towards the cleared level, never one line. A conflict starting within imminentS shows at once, one starting within warningS once confirmChecks of the last historyChecks checks found it; severity, wording, sound and the STCA yield are all keys here and in safetyNets.kinds.tct. regions are TopSky's TCT areas: each may override any setting, inhibit TCT, or with regionsOnly be the only places it runs. blindSpot is the menu probe built on it. OFF unless this section is authored, as STCA is. Every default is TopSky's. .dev tct-info prints the branch and band of an aircraft and every pair the last check looked at.

enabled.description: False stops the net evaluating. Use safetyNets.show.tct instead to keep it evaluating and hide it on this system.

lookaheadS.description: How far ahead each trajectory is predicted, TopSky's 300 s. The TCT simulations ran eight minutes, so 600 is the cap. A conflict starting after warningS never shows, but the probe runs on so its closest point and end are known.

stepS.description: Sample step of both predictions; must divide lookaheadS. The closest point inside a conflict is solved between samples, so a coarser step costs only the start time's resolution.

cadenceS.description: Seconds between checks, inside the 2 Hz position batch.

imminentS.description: A conflict starting within this shows at once, at severity 2.

warningS.description: A conflict starting between imminentS and this shows at severity 1 once confirmed. Must not exceed lookaheadS.

confirmChecks.description: TopSky's TCT_ConflictCount: how many of the last historyChecks checks must have found a warning-band conflict. A check counts only when one of the pair has a new position report since the last, because a check on the same two reports is one sample seen twice.

clearChecks.description: Counting checks without a conflict that clear a raised pair. A pair past its closest point and opening clears at once.

shortConflictS.description: The look-ahead study's hold: a warning-band conflict predicted to last under this many seconds AND never closer than shortConflictMarginNm inside the closing minimum waits for imminent. 0 switches it off.

shortConflictMarginNm.description: How far inside the closing minimum a short conflict may come and still be held: the study scopes the hold to the boundary (4 to 5 nm with a 5 nm minimum). A fast head-on pass on the centreline is never held.

lateralNm.description: The lateral minimum while the pair is closing.

lateralDivergingNm.description: The lateral minimum while the pair is opening. Must not exceed lateralNm.

verticalFt.description: The gap between the two vertical bands under which an instant is in conflict.

verticalUpperFt.description: The same where both bands are at or above FL410.

verticalUpperFromFl.description: Where the upper vertical minimum starts: a pair both of whose bands are at or above this flight level takes verticalUpperFt.

regions.description: Per-airspace minima in STCA's grammar, read by the same resolver so the two nets never disagree about which region a point is in. A rule overrides the minima it names; a rule naming lateralNm alone narrows the opening minimum to it. Where several match, the most conservative of each axis wins, and a pair takes the most conservative of its two aircraft.

sectorIds.description: Sector id globs, for example EGTT_LTC*. A trailing star is the only wildcard.

zoneTag.description: A tag on a zones.geojson polygon.

aboveFl.description: Applies at or above this flight level.

inhibit.description: TopSky's NoTCT: TCT does not look at an aircraft inside this area. The first matching area naming inhibit decides.

verticalUpperFt.description: This area's vertical minimum above verticalUpperFromFl.

warningS.description: This area's warning time, TopSky's TCTA_Alert_Times.

heading.description: An assigned heading, TopSky's TCT_AHDG_*. Believed while the track is within toleranceDeg of it, or until maxTurnS after the clearance; after that it is disbelieved and the route and ground track rules apply. The heading is taken as a track, with no wind and no magnetic variation.

reactionS.description: Seconds after the clearance on the present track before the turn starts.

turnRateDegS.description: The modelled turn rate onto the heading, the short way round.

route.description: Conformance to the expanded route, TopSky's TCT_Track_Tolerance and TCT_Waypoint_Turn_Radius. A conforming aircraft is flown waypoint to waypoint from the leg the route classifier picks, a direct-to already folded in, at the measured ground speed and with no turn radius.

toleranceDeg.description: The track against the bearing to the next waypoint.

toleranceNearWaypointDeg.description: The wider tolerance inside waypointRadiusNm of the previous or next waypoint.

vertical.description: The vertical band, TopSky's TCT_BS_* and TCTA_VS_*. At the cleared level, or level with none, the band is the current level. Level with a different cleared level it may start the change any time within leaveLevelS at any rate from minFpm to maxFpm. Climbing or descending it runs from (1 - minRatio) to (1 + maxRatio) times the measured rate, the top being maxFpm under thresholdFpm. It stops at the cleared level (a cleared ILS or visual approach is no level), else at the coordinated exit level, else the filed cruise level, the chain sectorExitLevel reads; with none it is unbounded and the explainer marks it assumed.

atLevelFt.description: Within this of the cleared level is at it: CAP 493's at a level.

levelFpm.description: Under this vertical rate the aircraft is read as level.

thresholdFpm.description: Below this measured rate the top of the band is maxFpm.

climb.description: TopSky's TCTA_VS_Climb: overrides minFpm, maxFpm and thresholdFpm for a climb.

thresholdFpm.description: Below this measured rate the top of the band is maxFpm.

descent.description: TopSky's TCTA_VS_Descent: overrides minFpm, maxFpm and thresholdFpm for a descent.

boundPreference.description: Which level the band stops at first when both exist: the cleared level, or the coordinated exit level (TopSky's TCT_Use_CFL_For_Coordinated off).

blindSpot.description: The Blind Spot values this area overrides, TopSky's BS_* fields on its TCTA lines.

verticalUpperFt.description: Blind Spot upper vertical minimum here.

windowS.description: Blind Spot window here, TopSky's BS_Warn. Never shorter than the pair's warningS plus cadenceS times confirmChecks.
